one_liner: Single-file MIT zlib/Deflate replacement with ZIP and PNG helpers; measured slower than zlib, chosen for portability, not speed.
what_it_does: miniz is an independent C implementation of Deflate (RFC 1951) and zlib (RFC 1950) streams, shipped as an amalgamated miniz.c/miniz.h pair or as a CMake/Meson module. It exposes a zlib-style API (mz_deflate/mz_inflate, mz_compress/mz_uncompress, crc32/adler32) under zlib's own names unless MINIZ_NO_ZLIB_COMPATIBLE_NAMES is defined, plus heap-free low-level coroutine codecs (tdefl compressor, tinfl decompressor), a ZIP reader/writer/appender and a PNG writer. Features can be compiled out with MINIZ_NO_* macros, down to just CRC-32 and Adler-32.
how_it_is_fast: It is not faster than zlib on any published measurement. The compressor uses the same hash-chaining LZ77 as zlib (32 KiB window, 2^15-entry hash, per-level probe counts from 1 at level 1 to 1500 at level 10, greedy parsing at levels 0-3) and has a special level-1 path, tdefl_compress_fast, that hashes 3-byte trigrams and compares 16-bit words. The decompressor is a single coroutine function with 10-bit fast Huffman lookup tables and a 64-bit bit buffer on 64-bit targets. CRC-32 is a plain 256-entry table loop, with no slicing-by-8 or carry-less multiply.
when_to_use: You need zlib-format compression or decompression in C or C++ with a single MIT-licensed source pair and no build-system dependency (embedded, games, tools).
You need simple ZIP read/write/append or a quick PNG writer alongside Deflate, without pulling in libzip or libpng.
Constrained or heap-free environments: tdefl/tinfl state structs can be memcpy-saved, the low-level codecs never allocate, and MINIZ_NO_MALLOC/TDEFL_LESS_MEMORY trim memory.
Streaming with tiny buffers: the coroutine design accepts input one byte at a time.
when_not_to_use: When speed is the goal: Wuffs measured miniz 2.2.0 decoding at 0.82-0.88x of zlib 1.2.11 (i5-10210U), and libdeflate, zlib-ng and ISA-L are all much faster than zlib on both sides.

gzip (.gz) streams or zlib features beyond the core: window_bits must be exactly 15 or -15, so gzip wrapping (31/47) and smaller windows are rejected, and there is no gz* file API, no deflateSetDictionary/inflateSetDictionary and no deflateParams.
Encrypted or multi-volume ZIP archives (unsupported per the README and header), or ZIP handling of untrusted archives where you cannot tolerate open bugs (see gotchas).
Multithreaded single-stream compression: it is single-threaded only.

Very large compressor counts in memory: by default each tdefl_compressor carries roughly 300 KB of fixed arrays (32 KiB dictionary, 64 KiB next-chain, 64 KiB hash, 64 KiB LZ code buffer, ~83 KiB output buffer; estimated from the struct fields).

integration.form: source-drop (amalgamated miniz.c + miniz.h from the releases page) or static/shared lib via CMake/Meson; header-only option via BUILD_HEADER_ONLY
integration.dependencies: none (libc only; stdio optional via MINIZ_NO_STDIO)
integration.min_toolchain: C90 (CMake sets CMAKE_C_STANDARD 90); also compiles as C++; tested with GCC, Clang and MSVC per README
integration.platforms: any; little-endian and 64-bit detection is automatic, big-endian handled in portable paths
integration.thread_safety: Separate mz_stream / tdefl / tinfl / mz_zip_archive objects can be used on separate threads; the header notes the ZIP m_last_error functionality is not thread safe; no global mutable state documented otherwise
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: zlib names and the common deflate/inflate/compress/uncompress/crc32/adler32 calls work (README says tested with libpng and libzip), but no gzip wrapper, no custom window sizes, no dictionaries, no deflateParams and no gz* file I/O; it reports its version as "11.3.2" through ZLIB_VERSION

gotchas: Since 3.0.0 MINIZ_USE_UNALIGNED_LOADS_AND_STORES defaults to 0 on every CPU, which compiles out the level-1 fast compressor (tdefl_compress_fast) and the 64-bit bit-writer path; the header itself says to set it to 1 for best performance. If you define it to 1 yourself, MINIZ_UNALIGNED_USE_MEMCPY is not defined, so the code falls back to raw pointer-cast loads (undefined behaviour under strict aliasing and UBSan); define both.

Open ZIP-layer bugs as of 2026-10: issue 387 (EOCD back-scan signed/unsigned promotion yields a negative file offset), 384 (mz_zip_reader_extract_iter_new frees a non-heap pointer on OOM for in-memory archives), 378 (central-directory offset overflow on zip64), 349 (pointer corruption on bigger files) and 330 (wrong extraction tied to file-position handling). The 3.1.2 changelog fixes a central-directory offset overflow and a code_len==0 infinite loop in tinfl_decompress and adds fuzz targets.

32-bit targets: issue 371 reported tinfl_decompress writing past the struct and output buffer on ESP32-S3 (32-bit bit buffer changes the fast-path refill cadence); it is closed, but no fixing commit was shown on the page, so over-allocate or test on 32-bit before trusting it. Issue 373 (claimed heap overflow in code-length RLE) is closed; the current m_len_codes array is padded by 137 bytes, which covers the largest run (counter <= 319 plus up to 138).
Using zlib and miniz in one binary causes symbol clashes unless MINIZ_NO_ZLIB_COMPATIBLE_NAMES is defined; on glibc, define _LARGEFILE64_SOURCE before including miniz.c or ZIP files over 2 GB fail.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick miniz over zlib-ng or libdeflate only when a single-file, C90, MIT-licensed codec with built-in ZIP/PNG helpers matters more than speed; for throughput, libdeflate (1.44-1.74x zlib on the same Wuffs runs) or zlib-ng are the catalogued choices, and LZ4 or zstd if you do not need the Deflate format.
verified_claims_summary: The README makes only directional claims (levels 2-9 'designed to compare favorably against zlib's ratio and speed'; level 1 about 35% slower than minilzo with 5-9% better ratio) and its referenced performance page was not located. The only independent numbers, Wuffs doc/benchmarks.md (Core i5-10210U, Debian Bullseye builds, Wuffs commit 315b2e52), show miniz 2.2.0 decoding raw deflate at 204/252/287 MB/s versus zlib 1.2.11 at 241/289/352 MB/s (1k/10k/100k, 0.82-0.87x) and zlib streams at 237/272 versus 268/323 MB/s (0.84-0.88x); compression speed versus zlib is unmeasured.
status_note: Actively maintained (last commit 2026-07-01, 3.1.x line with fuzz targets and Catch2 tests) and MIT-licensed, so it is easy to vendor, but it belongs in the catalog for portability and convenience, not for beating zlib.
